raw_response:
I farm this land the way I always have to keep the family steady. Wheat and maize are my main way, because one follows the other and that is safer for me. I know this 12.4 mu, and after so many years I trust what I have seen more than what people say on paper. I cannot gamble much because some people in the house work outside and cash is never loose for long. So for wheat I will do the usual timing in October, use the seed we can get easily in town, put enough fertilizer so the crop does not turn weak, and give water a few times from the well if the sky stays dry. After wheat comes off in June, I will hurry to plant maize right away, because if you miss those few days you lose yield. I do not want too much tillage between the two crops, just enough to get the maize in fast. For stevia, I keep a smaller area because it brings cash but it is more troublesome than grain, and I do not want too much risk or too much hand work. I will manage it more carefully, but not spend too much money unless it looks promising.

I still do things in a plain way: a bit heavy on fertilizer rather than too light, because if you save a little money and the crop goes hungry, then you lose more at harvest. But I also cannot spend without limit. So I keep the grain crops on the bigger area, use family labor first, hire only a little when work comes all at once, and use the well when the crop really needs it.
